newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Uneximbank to bid for 51 pct in Sibneft.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Uneximbank to bid for 51 pct in Sibneft.

text.p: Russia's third biggest bank by assets, Uneximbank, will bid on Wednesday for a 51 percent stake in Russia's seventh biggest oil group Sibneft, a bank spokesman said on Tuesday.
Modest Kolerov told Reuters that Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian) would bid together with its investment partner KM-Invest, which would be an intermediary in the deal.
"For Uneximbank participation in the tender is as important for its investment business development as the one Uneximbank-MFK group is carrying out on SIDANKO," he said.
The Interros group, built around Uneximbank and Bank MFK, already owns about 85 percent of Russia's fifth biggest oil group SIDANKO.
Uneximbank also controls a 38 percent stake, with 51 percent of the voting shares, in Norilsk Nickel metals producer under the government shares-for-loans deal.

Fifty one percent of shares in OAO Sibirskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (Sibneft) is on offer at an investment tender on May 12. Foreign bidders are not allowed to participate, as foreign investors are generally limited to 15 percent of Russian companies.
The starting price of the stake is $101 million.

The winner must also pay $40 million within a year after the contract is signed, pay off $10 million of Sibneft and its subsidiaries debts within six months, and pay $49 million in seven-year rent payments for Sibneft's Moscow office or provide the company with a similar building.
Another condition is a transfer of 13 percent of shares in AO Noyabrskgeofizika prospecting company, which will provide Sibneft with a stake of over 50 percent in Noyabrskgeofizika.
The 51 percent stake of 2.30 billion shares with a face value of 1.6 roubles was won by ZAO Neftyanaya Finansovaya Kompaniya (NFK) in 1995 under the shares-for-loans scheme.
NFK, which offered a $100.3 million credit to the government, is headed by businessman Boris Berezovsky, currently President Boris Yeltsin's deputy security adviser.
Uneximbank also has close links to the government. Its head, Vladimir Potanin, was until recently seconded from the bank to work as First Deputy Prime Minister in charge of economic policy.
Sibneft's main production unit is Noyabrskneftegaz, and its authorised capital is 7.23 billion roubles.

In 1996 ZAO Rifile-Oil won 15 percent of Sibneft shares and ZAO Sins won 19 percent of shares. The ownership of these two companies has not been published. An unknown foreign investor won 0.72 percent of shares.
Sibneft's chairman is Rem Vyakhirev, who also chairs gas monopoly RAO Gazprom.
